CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-plugin-side.md and research-prd-section-17.md §17.5.2, shell.lua owns module-level state { proc, stdin, stdout, rx_buf, gen, inflight, shell, driver, cwd, pending_cb }. It reads config + descriptor FRESH at call time (require("pi-bridge").config.shell, require("pi-bridge").bridge.server_info or M.get_shell_info()). The gen-guard mirrors completion.lua's two-layer supersession (state.gen monotonic counter).
2. INPUT: M.get_shell_info() from P2.M1.T1.S4 (provides descriptor.shell/shellSource/shellPath). require("pi-bridge").config.shell from P2.M3.T6.S1 (config block — but can default to { prefer="pi" } if not yet configured).

Returns (shell_path, source). Check config.shell.drivers for user-disabled drivers; (c) `pick_driver(resolved_shell)` -> basename via `resolved_shell:gsub(".*/","")` -> pcall(require, "pi-bridge.shell."..base) -> return drv if it has .start, else nil (degrade); (d) `M.session_cwd()` -> reads descriptor.cwd (from require("pi-bridge").descriptor or bridge.server_info.cwd). Read config + descriptor FRESH at call time (not cached at module load).

subtasks.title: ensure(on_ready) — spawn via vim.uv.spawn + driver delegation
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.5.2 skeleton, ensure(on_ready) spawns the daemon if not already running. It calls resolve_shell + pick_driver, then delegates to driver.start() which spawns the actual shell process. The daemon is a child of nvim (vim.uv.spawn), NOT of pi. If spawn fails, state.driver=nil and cb("error"). startup_timeout_ms (default 5000) guards cold-start.
2. INPUT: resolve_shell/prefer and pick_driver from P2.M1.T2.S2. Driver modules (fish/zsh/bash) export start(opts, on_ready) — the fish driver from P2.M2.T4.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement M.ensure(on_ready): if state.proc then return on_ready(nil) (already running). Read config fresh: `local cfg = require("pi-bridge").config.shell or {}`. Call resolve_shell(cfg.prefer or "pi"). Call pick_driver. If no driver -> on_ready("no driver for "..shell). Call state.driver.start({ shell=resolved, cwd=M.session_cwd(), startup_timeout_ms=cfg.startup_timeout_ms or 5000 }, function(err, proc, stdin, stdout) — on success: store proc/stdin/stdout in state, start stdout read_start with _feed callback, call on_ready(nil). On error: state.driver=nil, on_ready(err). Every uv call pcall'd. If state.failed (daemon previously crashed) -> short-circuit on_ready("daemon disabled").
4. OUTPUT: M.ensure(on_ready) spawns the daemon on first call, caches it. Subsequent calls are instant.
5. MOCKING: Tests use a fake driver module (exports start that calls on_ready with fake proc/pipes). Test: first call spawns, second call reuses, spawn error sets driver=nil.
6. DOCS: none — internal lifecycle, documented in the module header docstring from P2.M1.T2.S2.

subtasks.title: request(line, cursor, after, cb) — framed protocol + gen-guard supersession
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.5.1, the request payload is `__PIREQ__\t{json}\n` where json = { line, cursor (byte offset), after }. Per §17.5.2, supersession mirrors completion.lua: state.gen bumped per request, captured in the response callback. One in-flight request at a time (shell completion is fast; sentinel protocol is sequential). Per-request timeout (config.shell.timeout_ms, default 1500) via uv timer.
2. INPUT: M.ensure from P2.M1.T2.S3. state.gen from P2.M1.T2.S2.
3. LOGIC: Implement M.request(line, cursor, after, cb): call M.ensure(function(err) — if err return cb(err). Bump state.gen, capture local gen. Set state.inflight=true. Store state.pending_cb = function(items, prefix) with gen-guard: `if gen ~= state.gen then return end; state.inflight=false; cb(nil, items, prefix)`. Encode payload: `vim.json.encode({ line=line, cursor=cursor, after=after or "" })`. Write to stdin: `state.stdin:write(string.format("__PIREQ__\t%s\n", payload))`. Arm a uv timer for cfg.timeout_ms (default 1500) that fires pending_cb("timeout", {}, "") if not yet resolved (gen-guard drops it if superseded). pcall the write; on write failure call cb("write failed").
4. OUTPUT: M.request(line, cursor, after, cb) sends a framed request and calls cb(err, items, prefix) on response. Late responses for stale keystrokes are dropped by the gen-guard.
5. MOCKING: Tests use a fake driver that captures the written payload and calls back with canned responses. Test: sequential requests return correct items; a late response for gen=1 is dropped when gen=2 is current.
6. DOCS: none — internal protocol, documented in module header.

subtasks.title: _feed(chunk) buffering + sentinel slicing + JSON decode + normalize to AutocompleteItem[]
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.5.1, the plugin buffers stdout, slices between `__PIRESP_START__\n` and next `__PIRESP_END__\n`, vim.json.decode's the payload. Anything outside sentinels (prompts, async segments, stray output) is discarded. Per §17.5.2, _feed appends chunk to rx_buf, scans for sentinel pairs, extracts JSON, decodes (pcall'd), normalizes to AutocompleteItem[] { value, label, description? }, calls state.pending_cb (gen-guarded). Leftover stays in rx_buf.
2. INPUT: Raw stdout chunks from the daemon pipe (vim.uv read_start callback). The AutocompleteItem shape from completion.lua L246-252: { value: string, label: string, description?: string }.
3. LOGIC: Implement M._feed(chunk): if not chunk then M._reset() return end (EOF -> teardown). Append chunk to state.rx_buf. While rx_buf contains both __PIRESP_START__ and __PIRESP_END__: extract the substring between them (after __PIRESP_START__\n up to __PIRESP_END__\n). pcall(vim.json.decode, payload). If decode fails: increment state.parse_failures; if >= N (config or 5): mark state.failed=true, M.teardown(), notify once. If decode succeeds: normalize items: for each item { value, description? } -> { value=value, label=value, description=description }. Derive prefix client-side: last whitespace-delimited token of line[1..cursor]. Call state.pending_cb(items, prefix) if set. Remove processed bytes from rx_buf. All decode/parse pcall'd.
4. OUTPUT: M._feed(chunk) correctly parses daemon responses and calls the pending callback with normalized items.
5. MOCKING: Tests feed canned response strings (with sentinels, JSON payloads, noise outside sentinels). Assert items are parsed correctly. Test: noise/prompt output between sentinels is discarded. Test: malformed JSON increments parse_failures.
6. DOCS: none — internal parsing, documented in module header.

subtasks.title: teardown() — uv.process_kill SIGKILL, close pipes, reset state
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.5.2, teardown kills the proc (uv.process_kill SIGKILL), closes stdin/stdout pipes, resets state. It is called from VimLeavePre/ExitPre (P2.M3.T6.S3) and on N consecutive parse failures (§17.12). Must be idempotent (safe to call twice).
2. INPUT: state.proc/stdin/stdout from P2.M1.T2.S3.
3. LOGIC: Implement M.teardown(): if state.proc then pcall(uv.process_kill, state.proc, "sigkill") end. if state.stdin then pcall(state.stdin.close, state.stdin) end. if state.stdout then pcall(state.stdout.close, state.stdout); pcall(state.stdout.read_stop, state.stdout) end. Reset state: state.proc=nil, state.stdin=nil, state.stdout=nil, state.rx_buf="", state.gen=0, state.inflight=false, state.driver=nil. If state.pending_cb then state.pending_cb("teardown", {}, "") end. Idempotent — all nil-guarded.
4. OUTPUT: M.teardown() cleanly kills the daemon and resets state. Safe to call from VimLeavePre.
5. MOCKING: Tests spawn a real fish process, call teardown, assert no leaked uv handles (use vim.uv.loop():gc_collect() or handle count assertion).
6. DOCS: none — internal lifecycle.

subtasks.title: shell.complete_current(buf, cb) — read buffer, strip bangs, byte offsets, call shell.request
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.7, shell.complete_current(buf, cb) reads the buffer + cursor, strips the leading bangs (! or !!), computes line/cursor/after using BYTE offsets (NOT UTF-16 — no coords.lua conversion per §17.14). It then calls shell.request(line, cursor, after, cb). The cursor byte offset comes directly from nvim_win_get_cursor(0) which returns 0-based byte column.
2. INPUT: shell.request from P2.M1.T2.S4. The buffer and cursor from nvim API.
3. LOGIC: Implement M.complete_current(buf, cb) in shell.lua: (a) Read lines: `local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, false)`. (b) Read cursor: `local row, byte_col = unpack(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0))` — row is 1-based, byte_col is 0-based BYTE. (c) Get line 1: `local line1 = lines[1] or ""`. (d) Strip bangs: `local bangs = line1:sub(1,2) == "!!" and 2 or 1`; `local stripped = line1:sub(bangs + 1)`. (e) Compute cursor offset into stripped line: `local cursor = math.max(0, byte_col - bangs)` (byte offset, 0-based). (f) Compute after: `local after_text = stripped:sub(cursor + 1)` (text after cursor). (g) line for daemon = stripped:sub(1, cursor) (up to cursor). (h) Call `M.request(line_up_to_cursor, cursor, after_text, cb)`. All nvim API calls pcall'd; on error call cb("read error").
4. OUTPUT: M.complete_current(buf, cb) extracts the shell command from the buffer and calls M.request with byte-correct offsets.
5. MOCKING: Tests create a scratch buffer with "!git ch", set cursor position, call complete_current, assert the request payload has line="git ch" cursor=4 (after stripping "!").
6. DOCS: none — internal integration function.

subtasks.title: Notices — mismatch (§17.4.3), first-run hint (§17.9), degrade notify
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per architecture/research-plugin-side.md, notify.lua provides M.once(category, level, msg) — a dedup'd, vim.schedule-wrapped one-time notify. Categories are string keys in a seen={} set. M.reset() clears the set. M.did_notify(category) checks if already fired. This is the exact mechanism to reuse for all three shell notices.
2. INPUT: resolve_shell result from P2.M1.T2.S2 (provides shell + source). vim.env.SHELL for mismatch detection.

LOGIC: Add three notice calls using notify.once with distinct categories: (a) MISMATCH (§17.4.3): when prefer=="pi" resolves to bash (tier-2) AND $SHELL is zsh/fish (tier-1) AND that shell exists on PATH (vim.fn.executable). Category "shell_mismatch". Message: "pi runs commands in bash; using bash completion to match. For your native <SHELL> completions, set pi's shellPath to <SHELL>. :help pi-bridge-shell". Fire in resolve_shell or ensure after resolution. (b) FIRST-RUN (§17.9): the first time a "!" line is detected in a session. Category "shell_first_run". Message: "Shell completion active (<resolved shell>); :help pi-bridge-shell". Fire in complete_current on first call. Suppressed if daemon failed (the degrade notice fires instead). (c) DEGRADE (§17.12/§17.6.4): when the daemon fails to spawn or the driver is nil. Category "shell_degrade". Message: "Shell completion not available: <error>. !/!! commands will run normally." Fire in ensure on error.

subtasks.title: fish.lua driver startup script + start(opts, on_ready) + cd(path) exports
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.6.1, fish exposes `complete -C "<line>"` returning `word<TAB>description` lines using ALL loaded completions. The driver writes a startup script to a temp file (sourced via `fish -i`). `fish --noconfig` is WRONG — we WANT the user's config. The script binds a handler that reads __PIREQ__ lines, runs complete -C, and emits __PIRESP_START__/__PIRESP_END__ with JSON-escaped values (fish's `string escape --style=json`). The driver spawns via vim.uv.spawn with pipes.
2. INPUT: opts table from shell.lua ensure(): { shell="/usr/bin/fish", cwd=<pi cwd>, startup_timeout_ms=5000 }.
3. LOGIC: Create lua/pi-bridge/shell/fish.lua. Export M.start(opts, on_ready): (a) Write a fish startup script to a temp file (vim.fn.tempname()..".fish") containing: a `function __pi_handle` that reads a line, strips `__PIREQ__\t` prefix, parses JSON (or uses fish string ops to extract line/cursor), runs `complete -C "$cmd"`, iterates results emitting `{"value":...,"description":...}` JSON lines between sentinels, then `echo __PIRESP_END__`. A `function fish_prompt; end` to silence the prompt. A bind to trigger __pi_handle on each newline. (b) Spawn `fish -i` (NOT --noconfig) via vim.uv.spawn with the script sourced, stdin/stdout as pipes. (c) on_ready(err, proc, stdin, stdout) callback. (d) Export M.cd(path): write a `cd "<path>"` command to stdin to re-cd the daemon when pi's cwd changes. pcall all uv calls. startup_timeout via uv timer.
4. OUTPUT: fish.lua driver that shell.lua's pick_driver loads via require("pi-bridge.shell.fish"). Spawns a persistent fish subshell that responds to framed completion requests.
5. MOCKING: Integration test spawns real fish (/usr/bin/fish available). Sends `git ch` request, asserts checkout/cherry in response. Test gated on fish executable.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Docstring on fish.lua explaining: Tier 1 status, why fish -i (not --noconfig — we want user config), the complete -C technique, and the sentinel framing.

The Lua parsing in _feed (shell.lua P2.M1.T2.S5) handles the JSON payload between sentinels. But the fish DRIVER is responsible for emitting valid JSON. The prefix is derived client-side (last whitespace-delimited token of line[1..cursor]).

For description-less items, emit just {"value":...}. The _feed function in shell.lua (P2.M1.T2.S5) then vim.json.decode's the payload and normalizes to AutocompleteItem[] = { value=word, label=word, description=desc }. subtasks.title: accept.lua — current shell word computation + per-shell quoting table
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.8, shell candidates are plain words (NOT pi AutocompleteItems). Accept replaces the current shell word (not the whole buffer) using nvim_buf_set_text (range edit, not nvim_buf_set_lines). The current word = maximal substring of line[1..cursor] ending at cursor, delimited by unquoted whitespace. Per-shell quoting: fish wraps paths with spaces in double quotes; bash/zsh single-quote unless the candidate contains a single quote (then the '..."'"'...' idiom). Shell path uses BYTE offsets (no UTF-16 / coords.lua).
2. INPUT: The AutocompleteItem selected by the user (from menu.get_selected()). The resolved shell (from shell.lua state.shell) to determine quoting rules. The buffer + cursor position.
3. LOGIC: Create lua/pi-bridge/shell/accept.lua. Export M.accept(buf, item): (a) Read line 1 + cursor: `local row, col = unpack(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0))` — col is 0-based byte. (b) Compute current shell word: scan backward from col for unquoted whitespace. Quote-aware splitter: track open single/double quotes; break on whitespace outside quotes. word_start = byte offset where the word begins. (c) Quote the candidate value per shell: if shell basename is "fish": wrap in double quotes if it contains spaces. If bash/zsh: single-quote unless value contains a single quote (then use '..."'"'...' concatenation idiom). (d) Return { quoted_text=..., word_start_byte=..., cursor_byte=... } for P2.M2.T4.S4 to apply.
4. OUTPUT: M.accept(buf, item) computes the quoted text and the byte range to replace.
5. MOCKING: Tests create scratch buffers with various cursor positions. Table-test quoting: spaces, $, backtick, single quote, double quote, combined. Assert the quoted output and byte range.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Docstring on accept.lua explaining: local word-replacement (NOT pi's applyCompletion), per-shell quoting rules, and why nvim_buf_set_text (range edit, no TextChangedI re-entrancy).

subtasks.title: accept.lua — nvim_buf_set_text range edit + cursor positioning + re-trigger logic
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.8, step 3: replace bytes [word_start+1 .. cursor] (Lua 1-indexed) via nvim_buf_set_text(buf, row, start_col, row, end_col, {text}). This is a RANGE edit (not whole-buffer rewrite like pi-mode's nvim_buf_set_lines). nvim_buf_set_text does NOT fire TextChangedI for typed-input semantics, so no re-entrancy loop. Step 4: position cursor after inserted text, stay in Insert mode. Step 5: re-trigger fetch only if candidate ends in "/" (dir), else close menu.
2. INPUT: The quoted text + byte range from P2.M2.T4.S3. The buffer + cursor position. menu.close() from menu.lua.
3. LOGIC: Extend M.accept(buf, item) from P2.M2.T4.S3: (a) Apply the edit: `vim.api.nvim_buf_set_text(buf, row-1, word_start_byte, row-1, cursor_byte, { quoted_text })` (nvim API is 0-based row, 0-based col). pcall it; on failure insert raw value unquoted and notify once. (b) Position cursor: `vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { row, word_start_byte + #quoted_text })` — immediately after inserted text. Stay in Insert mode (do not mode-switch). (c) Re-trigger: if quoted_text ends with "/" (directory), call completion.refresh(buf) to re-fetch (shell will complete inside the directory). Else call menu.close() to close the completion menu. (d) Return true on success.
4. OUTPUT: M.accept(buf, item) replaces the current shell word with the quoted candidate, positions the cursor, and re-triggers or closes the menu.
5. MOCKING: Tests create a scratch buffer with "!git che", position cursor after "che", call accept with {value="checkout"}. Assert the buffer now reads "!git checkout" and cursor is positioned correctly. Test directory re-trigger (value ends with "/").
6. DOCS: none — accept behavior documented in accept.lua header docstring from P2.M2.T4.S3.

subtasks.title: zsh.lua capture-completion driver — zle widget, compinit, compadd redefinition
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.6.2, zsh has no compgen. The canonical technique (fzf's zsh completion + Valodim/zsh-capture-completion): a persistent interactive `zsh -f -i` with `autoload -Uz compinit && compinit -u`, a bound zle widget __pi_capture that programmatically drives the completion system by setting BUFFER/CURSOR and redefining compadd to collect word<TAB>desc into stdout between sentinels. This is the MOST FRAGILE driver — the exact zle incantation varies subtly across zsh versions. A spike (folded into this task) MUST validate against the installed zsh (/usr/bin/zsh). :checkhealth reports the detected zsh version.
2. INPUT: opts table from shell.lua ensure(): { shell="/usr/bin/zsh", cwd=<pi cwd>, startup_timeout_ms=5000 }.
3. LOGIC: Create lua/pi-bridge/shell/zsh.lua. Export M.start(opts, on_ready): (a) Write a zsh startup script to temp file containing: `autoload -Uz compinit && compinit -u`; define `__pi_capture()` widget that redefines `compadd` locally to `printf '%s\t%s\n' "$w" "$desc"` for each word, then calls `zle complete-word` (or the _main_complete entrypoint) with BUFFER/CURSOR set from the request; emit __PIRESP_START__ before and __PIRESP_END__ after; `zle -N __pi_capture`. A read loop that parses __PIREQ__ lines and triggers the widget. (b) Spawn `zsh -f -i` via vim.uv.spawn with pipes. (c) SPIKE: before finalizing, write a standalone test that spawns zsh, sources the script, sends `git ch`, and validates checkout/cherry appear. Adjust the widget incantation until it works with the installed zsh version. (d) Export M.cd(path): write `cd "<path>"` to stdin. pcall all uv calls.
4. OUTPUT: zsh.lua driver that shell.lua's pick_driver loads via require("pi-bridge.shell.zsh"). Captures completions via the zle widget.
5. MOCKING: Integration test spawns real zsh (/usr/bin/zsh available). Sends `git ch`, asserts checkout/cherry appear. Test gated on zsh executable. The spike validates the exact invocation.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Docstring on zsh.lua explaining: Tier 1 status, the capture-completion technique (redefined compadd), fragility note (zle varies across versions), and the compinit requirement.

subtasks.title: bash.lua best-effort driver — COMP_* vars, compgen/compspec, bash-completion sourcing
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per research-prd-section-17.md §17.6.3, compgen returns BARE WORDS, NO DESCRIPTIONS (documented limitation). A bare bash -c does NOT source the user's completion library. The driver sources bash-completion best-effort and invokes the registered -F completion function for the command word if present, else compgen -f -d (files+dirs). COMP_LINE/COMP_POINT/COMP_WORDS/COMP_CWORD are set per request. Opt-out via drivers.bash = false.
2. INPUT: opts table from shell.lua ensure(): { shell="/usr/bin/bash", cwd=<pi cwd>, startup_timeout_ms=5000 }.
3. LOGIC: Create lua/pi-bridge/shell/bash.lua. Export M.start(opts, on_ready): (a) Write a bash rcfile to temp containing: best-effort sourcing of /usr/local/etc/bash_completion and /etc/bash_completion; a `__pi_complete()` function that sets COMP_LINE/COMP_POINT/COMP_WORDS/COMP_CWORD from the request, checks for a registered `-F` completion fn via `complete -p "$cmd"`, invokes it if present (fills COMPREPLY), else `compgen -f -d -- "$cur"`; emits each COMPREPLY entry as {"value":...} JSON between sentinels. A read loop for __PIREQ__ lines. (b) Spawn `bash --rcfile <this> -i` via vim.uv.spawn with pipes. (c) Export M.cd(path). pcall all uv calls. (d) JSON encoding: use printf piped through a safe encoder, or emit raw words and let Lua-side _feed wrap them.
4. OUTPUT: bash.lua driver loaded via require("pi-bridge.shell.bash"). Returns bare words (no descriptions). Files/dirs always work.
5. MOCKING: Integration test spawns real bash (/usr/bin/bash available). Tests: `!ls /tm` -> /tmp/ entries; git compspec iff bash-completion present (skip otherwise). Test gated on bash executable.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Docstring on bash.lua explaining: Tier 2 status, bare-words limitation (no descriptions), bash-completion dependency, and the opt-out via drivers.bash=false.
